_note: good.md, none-link.md, gate-good.md, gate-glob-good.md, gate-doc-only.md (a markdown file is not a gate file unless it is owner-only: gate-owner-markdown.md edits a skill and has no Gate changes section), gate-base-rule-good.md and gate-none.md, followup-filed.md, followup-in-code.md and followup-denied.md (it says no follow-ups and names /log-followup) pass. placeholder.md is the shipped PR template, unfilled: its example command and #123 live in comments and must not count. A `<name>.changes.json` beside a body lists what that PR changed; the gate-* cases are read against the harness's gate paths. A sidecar's `globs` are the gate paths the base branch's harness listed: a PR that removes a rule is held to it. One line may name a directory glob (`ci/fixtures/known-bad/p1/**`): it covers the files it matches and nothing else. A sidecar's `links` are the symlinks and submodule links the PR adds, removes or changes: each is a gate change (#149); a sidecar without that list is unreadable. gate-gitattributes.md and gate-gitmodules.md each change one of git's own settings files, which the harness guard counts and no harness rule names (#174), and have no Gate changes section. A `<!--` closed by a `-->` beyond a heading may be a comment or two marks written as text, and the check cannot tell which, nor where a section ends (#189): the body gets that one finding and nothing else in it is read. gate-comment-mark.md has the marks in inline code and every gate file on its own line; gate-swallowed-heading.md has the same marks and names a gate file only in a later section; gate-hidden-section.md wraps its whole Gate changes section in a comment. part-of-open-unsaid.md says `Part of #31`, closes nothing, lists a run as not verified and says nothing about #31 staying open (#241): its finding leads with closing the issue the PR finished, then the owed section, then `leaves #n open`. part-of-owed.md (the section alone), part-of-leaves-open.md (the sentence alone) and part-of-closes.md (a closing link beside `Part of`) pass. part-of-leaves-other.md leaves open an issue it is not part of. part-of-bold-link.md writes its `Part of` in bold, with the issue as a link. part-of-quoted-answers.md only quotes its answers: a closing link in inline code and in an indented block, the sentence in inline code, the section inside a code block, and a closing word before #0. part-of-after-mark.md writes its `Part of` in a leading `---` block, above a comment opener and a one-line fence written as text, where a reader of prose alone would lose it; prose-only.md says it leaves #4 open, so it keeps its one finding. followup-none-contradicted.md says Follow-ups is none and calls a deferred correction a follow-up in What (#242); followup-entry-unreferenced.md has one entry with an issue and one with neither an issue nor `not filed:`; followup-filed.md has one of each allowed form and still says follow-up in What; followup-in-code.md says follow-up only inside a code span and a code block. followup-nested-bullet.md defers work in a sub-bullet indented four spaces; followup-second-section.md has a second Follow-ups section whose entry names no issue.

details.part-of-open-unsaid.md#links/open-unsaid: closes nothing. If this PR finishes an issue, close it: `Closes #n`. If it leaves a check for after merge, add `## Owed after merge` and say which issue it leaves open. Only if it finishes nothing, say it `leaves #31 open`, and why
